About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Statistics and Data Science Year 13
subject of the New Zealand Curriculum. Equivalent for Te Marautanga o Aotearoa is
being published separately.

Progress and assessment information for Statistics and Data Science Year 13 is still
in development. Once that is completed, Statistics and Data Science Year 13 is
proposed to be made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum
Statement under section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Statistics and Data Science Year 13 will be required to start using it in
Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.




Statistics and Data Science | Year 13 | October 2026                                   Page 2

Purpose statement                                                   Ānō me he whare pūngāwerewere.   Behold, it is like the web of a spider.




  In Statistics and Data Science, students are taught how to collect, source,
  construct, and manage data ethically. They are taught to explore data with
  curiosity, and to build, analyse, interpret, and communicate findings from a wide
  range of statistical and computational models. Statistical and computational
  methods are employed using technology to support investigation, prediction, and
  decision-making.


Through the study of Statistics and Data Science, students are taught statistical and
data concepts and methods to collect, analyse, and represent data, and to use data
to make informed decisions. They explore data collection, management, and
stewardship, alongside their ability to interpret data and justify conclusions.

Statistics and Data Science provides students with the knowledge and practices to
investigate patterns, relationships, contributing factors, and impacts, while
maintaining data integrity. This disciplinary knowledge enables students to apply
concepts, techniques and models to data-rich situations while considering validity,
limitations, and ethical implications of data use.

As students progress through Statistics and Data Science Year 13, they are
supported to develop increasingly sophisticated abilities in communicating in written
form statistical thinking using data-based evidence. They become critical users of
data, evaluating models, conclusions, and generative AI outputs using evidence-
informed reasoning.

  Statistics and Data Science leads to pathways in data science, statistics,
  probability, and related fields like computer science, accounting, geography,
  business, health sciences, psychology, and other disciplines that rely on data-
  driven decision-making, and to further academic research.

The teaching of all knowledge and practices is compulsory. Schools can determine
how learning is organised across the year, including integrating content from multiple
elements and strands where this supports coherence and depth. Examples within the
teaching sequence and contexts in brackets signified by ‘e.g.’ are provided as
guidance only; provided the intended knowledge and practices are met, schools and
teachers may substitute contexts and examples that better reflect local environments,
iwi and hapū connections, student interests, and teacher expertise.

Disciplinary writing is included in the teaching sequence to provide clarity about what
subject-specific literacy is to be taught. Disciplinary writing is organised into a
knowledge component that is consistent across all year levels and a practice
component that is sequenced across years.
